candidate_sentences.text: Nordecon group reported financial results for the twelve months of 2025 showing a decrease in revenue and profitability compared to the previous year.
Total revenue for 2025 was 208,281 thousand euros, representing a decrease of approximately 7 percent from 223,925 thousand euros in 2024.
Gross profit for 2025 was 13,535 thousand euros, down from 16,770 thousand euros in 2024, resulting in a gross margin of 6.5 percent compared to 7.5 percent in the prior year.
Operating profit decreased to 5,651 thousand euros from 8,061 thousand euros, and the operating margin declined to 2.7 percent from 3.6 percent in 2024.
Net profit for the period was 2,545 thousand euros, compared to 5,165 thousand euros in 2024.

Net profit attributable to owners of the parent company was 1,439 thousand euros, down from 3,827 thousand euros, resulting in basic and diluted earnings per share of 0.05 euros compared to 0.12 euros in 2024.

Financial performance was negatively impacted by foreign exchange losses of 750 thousand euros resulting from the 12 percent weakening of the Ukrainian hryvnia against the euro, which affected loans provided to Ukrainian subsidiaries.

verified_key_information_units.information: Year-on-year segment revenue changes showed the Buildings segment decreasing approximately 10% while the Infrastructure segment increased approximately 10%, resulting in Buildings contributing 81% of total revenue (down from 84%) and Infrastructure 19% (up from 16%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key figures section; Segment reporting – operating segments (revenue tables)

candidate_sentences.text: The revenue decline was primarily driven by an approximate 10 percent drop in the buildings segment, whereas revenue in the infrastructure segment grew by 10 percent.
The buildings segment accounted for 81 percent of total revenue.

verified_key_information_units.information: The order book grew by 30% to €273.1m at year-end, driven by a nearly threefold increase in the Infrastructure segment order book; approximately 69% of the backlog relates to work scheduled for 2026, with the remainder spread across 2027-2028.

candidate_sentences.text: A significant positive development during the period was the substantial growth of the company order book.
At 31 December 2025, the order book stood at 273,060 thousand euros, representing an increase of approximately 30 percent compared to 209,489 thousand euros at the end of 2024.
This growth was driven by a nearly threefold increase in the infrastructure segment order book, bolstered by major contracts such as the Rail Baltica project and road construction assignments.

verified_key_information_units.information: Cash flows for 2025 included €1.2m net cash from operating activities, €2.8m net cash used in investing activities (including €2.9m placed in long-term deposits), and €1.2m net cash used in financing activities, resulting in a net cash outflow of €2.8m for the year.

Liquidity position at 31 December 2025 was characterized by a current ratio of 0.93 (down from 0.94 in 2024), cash and cash equivalents of €5.3m (down from €8.2m), and short-term borrowings of €12.0m.
